newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar signs $400 million deal for HBI plant.
newsitem.headline: Qatar signs $400 million deal for HBI plant.

text.p: Qatar Steel Company said on Tuesday it signed a $400 million revised partnership deal with Gulf and foreign firms to produce hot briquetted iron (HBI) after three Japanese companies pulled out.

Minister of Electricity and Water Ahmad Mohammad Ali al-Subaie, also Qatar Steel Company (QASCO) chairman, said three Qatari, two Kuwaiti and a Canadian firm will own Qatar Hot Briquetted Iron Company (QABICO).
It will produce two million tonnes of HBI - used in steel plants to make molten steel - from early 1999.
QASCO will retain 31 percent and Qatar Shipping Company and Qatar Industrial Manufacturing Company will each hold 10 percent of (QABICO).
Japan's Mitsubishi Corp, Mitsui Corp and Marubeni Corp had signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) in December to take a 10 percent stake each in the venture and part of its production.
But they pulled out of the project after a dispute over the amount of production they will take.

The three complained of "an unproportionate tilt" in favour of Canada's Duferco Participations Holding Ltd of Guernsey in the Channel Islands, which also holds a 10 percent stake, an industry source said.
According to the MOU signed on December 18 the three Japanese firms and Duferco were to take 1.2 million tonnes a year QASCO would take 400,000 tonnes. The rest would be sold in the market.
"As the MOU was not clear about the individual portions of the foreign shareholders in the output, differences arose when Duferco pressed for a lion's share", said the source.
Subaie expressed regret over the withdrawal of the Japanese companies but he said he was confident the move would have no negative impact on the project.

The shares of the Japanese have been distributed among the Kuwaiti partners - Gulf Investment Corporation and National Industries Company of Kuwait - and Duferco. Each of the three will now have 16.33 percent instead of 10 percent.
Duferco has now undertaken to buy all 1.2 million tonnes a year of HBI.
The project will use Qatar's abundant natural gas to operate.

Subaie told reporters QABICO's partners would raise 30 percent of the project's cost through equity and 70 percent will be financed by loans arranged by a consortium of eight local and international banks.
Financing would be put in place within three months, he added.
The eight banks are -- the partly state-owned Qatar National Bank, Sumitomo Bank, Banque Paribas, Credit Suisse, Chase Manhattan, ANZ Grindlays, Arab Banking Corporation and Gulf International Bank.
